definitions.explanation: A medicine or drug that reduces or eliminates pain. The most common everyday word for over-the-counter and prescription pain medication.

examples.japanese: {痛|いた}み{止|ど}め⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}んだ→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
⟦{頭痛|ずつう}→頭痛：03369_zutsuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ひどい→ひどい：01097_hidoi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{痛|いた}み{止|ど}め⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: I have a bad headache, so please give me a painkiller.

examples.japanese: ⟦{医者|いしゃ}→医者：02847_isha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{痛|いた}み{止|ど}め⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{処方|しょほう}→処方：05976_shohou⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I had the doctor prescribe me a painkiller.

examples.japanese: {痛|いた}み{止|ど}め⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{切|き}れて→切れる：01936_kireru⟧、⟦また→また：00969_mata⟧⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}く→痛い：01108_itai⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧きた。
examples.english: The painkiller wore off, and my tooth started hurting again.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{痛|いた}み→痛み：01795_itami⟧ (pain, from the verb ⟦{痛|いた}む→痛む：03008_itamu⟧) and {止|ど}め (stopping, from the verb ⟦{止|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧), with the voicing change ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧→ど. Literally "pain-stopper." This is the standard everyday term for painkillers of any kind — the word learners are most likely to need at a pharmacy or doctor's office.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {痛|いた}み{止|ど}め⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧: to take a painkiller
- {痛|いた}み{止|ど}め⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{処方|しょほう}→処方：05976_shohou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to prescribe a painkiller
- {痛|いた}み{止|ど}め⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{効|き}く→効く：01932_kiku⟧: the painkiller takes effect
- {痛|いた}み{止|ど}め⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{切|き}れる→切れる：01936_kireru⟧: the painkiller wears off
- ⟦{市販|しはん}→市販：12424_shihan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{痛|いた}み{止|ど}め: over-the-counter painkiller

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{鎮痛剤|ちんつうざい}→鎮痛剤：15451_chintsuuzai⟧: analgesic — the more formal/medical term for the same thing
- {解熱鎮痛剤|げねつちんつうざい}: antipyretic analgesic — a fever reducer that also relieves pain
- ⟦{湿布|しっぷ}→湿布：15751_shippu⟧: compress/patch — a topical pain relief method rather than oral medication
